svg.aria-label: When the codex's sources were written
svg.text: Sixteen centuries of texts, and the proposed date read in the codex. The scale opens out after 1250, where most of them fall.

g.data-label: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews
g.data-desc: Written in Rome after the war. The codex tells the siege, Vespasian and Titus, and the mother who eats her child. The siege of jerusalem.

g.data-label: The Life of Adam and Eve
g.data-desc: A Jewish and Christian textual tradition preserved in Greek, Latin and other versions; its precise date and place of origin are disputed. The codex opens with it and runs it straight into the legend of the Rood. Adam, eve, seth and the branch.
The figure of the sun for the three Persons, in the endnotes. Sun, ray and the ray's tip.
The two pence as the two commandments of love, in the endnotes. The samaritan's two pence.
Montier-en-Der, Champagne. The birth of antichrist.
A Bulgarian apocryphon: Satanael sets up a throne of his own; Gabriel is sent and refuses, then Michael. The nearest cousin to the codex's Lucifer pages. The stolen robe, wreath and sceptre.
Recorded as a trap: the Grail cup was added to the poem in 1832. The codex's cup has no medieval Grail behind it. A stone from lucifer's crown.
Purgatorial punishments, no fire named.
Westminster. Also London: the King James Bible (1611), Whiston's Josephus (1737), Wake's apocryphal gospels (1820), the English Missal (1865). The english the legend is read in here.
Probably written by the Carthusian associated with Lovold; the exact place of composition is not certain. The branch promised, the healing deferred.
Melanchthon's preface carries the scheme the codex's end-of-world count belongs to. Six thousand years, in three spans.
A Catholic reader of 1593 is at least as much missal and breviary as it is scripture. The liturgy.
Challoner's revision (1750). The Bible this edition reads the codex against, because the compiler worked from the Vulgate. The catholic english of the vulgate.
The codex says its Passion is taken from Matthew and John, and most of its pages retell the gospels of the year. The compiler had them in the Vulgate. The passion, the parables, the acts.
The infancy gospel behind the Joachim and Anne cycle; its place of composition is debated. Pseudo-Matthew (probably 7th c., Latin) adds the Golden Gate. Joachim and anne.

Egyptian and surviving in Coptic, commonly understood as a third-century core with fourth-century Christian reworking. Enoch and Elijah are killed by the Antichrist and raised after three days and a half. Elijah addressed by the word of the lord.

The Latin legend of Heraclius humbled at the gate of Jerusalem, dated between the end of the seventh century and the middle of the eighth. Where it was written is not settled. Heraclius and the cross.
Greek, attributed to St John Damascene; the version behind the Latin ones is from Mount Athos around the year 1000. The apologue of the man in the well.
The great Latin legendary. The compiler had it in Latin; this edition reads it in Caxton's English. The rood, the finding of the cross, the saints.
Survives whole only in Church Slavonic, over twenty manuscripts; Coptic fragments exist. Its date of composition is disputed. Enoch writes 360 books.

g.data-label: The York, Chester, Towneley and N-Town plays
g.data-desc: Four distinct English dramatic collections, not a single York corpus; Towneley and N-Town cannot be securely pinned to one city. The mystery cycles.
Made for the Poor Clares at Obuda; kept in Debrecen since 1753. One of three Hungarian codices of the 1520s that carry the Seth episode. Seth at adam's grave, in hungarian.
The only telling named in the notes in which Adam is alive when Seth comes back, as the codex has it. Adam alive when seth returns.
Session 22, chapter 7 and canon 9. The water mixed with the wine.
The official Roman edition was promulgated in 1584, not with the Missal in 1570. 5,199 years to the nativity.
On Kiraly and Tokai's reading, one of the codex's last leaves gives 1593. Everything on this plate that is gold was in its compiler's reach in Latin or in Hungarian by then.

svg.text: what this edition read it against
